findings.summary: The four anomalies (dirty read, non-repeatable read, phantom, write skew) are used as the core vocabulary but never defined or illustrated, and the one example is not named as write skew.
findings.evidence: "Read Committed","blocks":"dirty read","allows":"non-repeatable" ... "Repeatable Read","+ non-repeatable","phantom, write skew"; the takeaway is "name the anomalies", yet the page defines none of them
findings.fix: Add a one-line definition per anomaly, or a small table with an example for each. Label the two-doctors example explicitly as write skew.

findings.summary: The handwritten margin note overlaps the title text and pink title block.
findings.evidence: The note "open once, reuse thousands of times" sits over the right end of the "Connection Pooling" title. The note "size to the DB!" also touches the title's top edge.
findings.fix: Shorten the title or its block so it ends before the note column. Alternatively, move the margin notes above the title row or drop one of them for this page.

findings.summary: The #sqlinterview hashtag targets SQL query-writing interviews, but the carousel covers system-design database concepts such as sharding and replication.
findings.evidence: hashtags include "#sqlinterview"; the content is Transactions, MVCC, Replication, Partitioning and Sharding
findings.fix: Replace #sqlinterview with a relevant tag such as #distributedsystems or #databasedesign.

findings.summary: The cover title doesn't match the series title, dropping both the count and the 'can't skip' framing.
findings.evidence: series: "10 DATABASE CONCEPTS YOU CAN'T SKIP IN SYSTEM DESIGN INTERVIEWS" vs titles[0]: "Database Concepts for System Design Interviews"
findings.fix: Rename the cover title to "10 Database Concepts You Can't Skip in System Design Interviews" so it matches the series title and the caption's '10 database concepts' opener.

findings.summary: The takeaway tells the learner to name the saga pattern, but sagas and 2PC are never explained or illustrated.
findings.evidence: "Spans __one database__; cross-service needs sagas or 2PC" and "name the ==saga pattern== across services"
findings.fix: Add a one-line definition of a saga (a sequence of local transactions with compensating undo steps), with a tiny example such as order, payment, refund.

findings.summary: The ACID mechanism table relies on locks, MVCC, WAL and fsync before any of them is taught or defined. Locking and MVCC come on pages 7-8, and WAL is only mentioned in passing on page 10.
findings.evidence: "Isolation","No interference","Locks / MVCC"; "WAL + fsync at COMMIT"
findings.fix: Add a one-line gloss for WAL (a log written before the data change) and fsync (force to disk). Add "covered on pages 7-8" next to Locks / MVCC.

findings.summary: CAP is referenced as a confusion point but CAP is never introduced in the handbook.
findings.evidence: "Mixing up ACID **C** with the **C** in CAP"
findings.fix: Add a short gloss, such as "CAP's C means all nodes return the same latest data", or drop the bullet.

findings.summary: The isolation table says Repeatable Read always allows phantoms. The SQL standard permits them, but PostgreSQL's Repeatable Read (snapshot isolation) and InnoDB's (next-key locks) largely prevent them. The page also names those two engines.
findings.evidence: ["Repeatable Read","+ non-repeatable","phantom, write skew"] and the cheatsheet row ["Serializable","+ phantom, write skew"]
findings.fix: Label the table "SQL standard minimum" and add a note that Postgres and InnoDB Repeatable Read avoid most phantoms but still allow write skew (Postgres) or lost updates.

findings.summary: The margin note touches the right edge of the title block.
findings.evidence: The note "how much can txns see?" starts at the edge of the pink "Isolation Levels" block, with the "h" of "how" abutting the block.
findings.fix: Narrow the title block or give the note column a left margin so the note clears the block.

findings.summary: The doctors example uses Repeatable Read and Serializable outcomes before the page explains what each level blocks.
findings.evidence: Heading "1. Two doctors off call" with result "Repeatable Read | both commit, 0 on call" precedes heading "2. What each level blocks"
findings.fix: Put the levels table first, then the doctors example as the worked case.

findings.summary: The MVCC example says txn 100 keeps reading 500 after txn 101 commits, but that only holds at Repeatable Read or higher, and no level is stated.
findings.evidence: "COMMIT; -- 100 still reads 500" and note "txn 100 sees 500 until it ends"
findings.fix: Add "BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ;" to txn 100, or note that at Read Committed the next statement would see 400.

findings.summary: The mode table introduces multi-leader replication before the page's single-primary model has been established with failover. Conflict resolution is never explained.
findings.evidence: "Multi-leader","local leader has it","needs conflict resolution" while the page says "one **primary** takes writes"
findings.fix: Remove the multi-leader row, or add a short note that it allows several writers and so produces write conflicts.

findings.summary: Consistent hashing is asserted as the fix for resharding with no example or explanation of how it works.
findings.evidence: "==Consistent hashing== lets you add a shard and move only about **1/N** of them."
findings.fix: Add a short example, such as keys on a ring where a new shard takes over only its neighbour's range, or a before/after count of moved keys.

findings.summary: The closing parenthesis is orphaned onto its own line in the table cell.

findings.fix: Widen the second column or shorten the text, for example "copies data: availability, reads (lag)".

findings.summary: Caching is presented as step 2 of the scaling order but is never defined or covered in the handbook.
findings.evidence: {"text":"2. Cache","ink":"green"} and the takeaway "index, cache, replicate, partition, and shard only last"
findings.fix: Add a one-line gloss for cache (an in-memory store such as Redis in front of the database), or state that it is outside the ten concepts.
